Causes of bacterial meningitis after 1 month?
Signs of meningitis in an infant?
Fever, poor feeding, irritability, high-pitched cry, bulging fontanelle, seizures.
Signs of meningitis in older children?
Headache, vomiting, photophobia, neck stiffness, Kernig and Brudzinski signs.
Glass test sign of meningococcal septicaemia?
Purpuric rash that does not blanch under a glass.
Clear, ≤ 5 lymphocytes, protein 0.15–0.4 g/L, glucose ~2/3 of blood.
Turbid, neutrophils, high protein, low glucose.
Clear, lymphocytes, normal glucose, normal/slightly high protein.
Lymphocytes, very high protein, low glucose, cobweb clot.
Low or falling GCS, focal signs, papilloedema, shock, bleeding disorder, local infection.
Should antibiotics wait for the LP?
No: blood culture then ceftriaxone at once.
0.15 mg/kg 6-hourly × 4 days, with or before first antibiotic.
Single-dose ciprofloxacin (or rifampicin, or ceftriaxone IM).
Persistent fever and bulging fontanelle on treatment?
Hib, pneumococcal conjugate, meningococcal (MenA conjugate, multivalent).
Most important treatable cause of encephalitis?
Aciclovir 20 mg/kg IV 8-hourly (21 days if confirmed).
